title: Bind sharper downset bounds to the rounded Full allocation
body:
The sharper `2 sqrt(N) (ΛQ)²` completed-downset theorem explicitly leaves its rounded Full-factory substitution open. This binds it to the actual caller using a one-expression authenticated allocation adapter, replacing the old `256 N³(ΛQ)^12` by the dyadic rational envelope `2 · 2^ceil(log2(N)/2) · (ΛQ)²`. The frozen Full implementation stays intact; every other allocation formula, admission guard, child compiler and same-stored-value inverse is retained.

The quantified proof re-establishes the normalized product perturbation, inverse/scalar margin, generator and physical-fragment envelope, coefficient/data split, incoming grid, amplitude and coefficient/temporary heights. It retains the block-solve theorem and original generator/rank contracts as explicit dependencies. At the actual non-Hermitian N=4 fixture, child precision falls 72→26 bits and data precision 76→61 bits while 189 actual layers meet the same forward/inverse target. These fixture savings are not a universal constant gain. No selected κ or physical preparation/delivery tariff changes.

Validation: registered warning-strict CPython 3.12 normal/optimized replay passes 63 parameter contracts, six actual factories and 24 actual forward/stored-inverse rounded trajectories. Cases include a tiny pivot, complex matrices, 512-bit incoming data and zero-layer shears. Seven controls cover source-expression drift, types/dimension, rounded-zero pivot, wrong stored-inverse order and an underfunded actual grid. Committed-byte/source-history and official 17-file export integrity pass. Git-free normal/optimized replay with `PATH=/nonexistent` passes (0.569/0.577 s locally), exported bytes remain unchanged, and corrupt live source rejects. Hosted CI has not yet been verified.

Three substantive commits separate the source-authenticated allocation/proof, independent actual-factory replay, and finalized evidence/contract metadata. Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4202#discussioncomment-19138298 . Base `b91956876e5b4122fd89179f1b57557ff8378f15`, priority revision 7. Entry overlap covered 317 open PRs, 4,064 discussion records and 6,636 current-base notes; no exhaustive novelty claim.

Credit Nick Petalas for the block-solve theorem, Brian's PR4788 for the earlier leading-section bridge, Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml for Full and its allocation/rounding theorem, Vlado/PR1673 for the compiler, Chafik/PR628 for certified phases, and retained Stein/interval source contributors. Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The proof is scoped to the stated source contracts; automated execution is not independent human or proof-kernel acceptance. Open next questions retain the normalized/raw caller and physical cost boundaries.

Submission checkpoint: fresh official main at 04:59 UTC remains `b91956876e5b4122fd89179f1b57557ff8378f15`, with unchanged guidance and affected source inputs. Complete submission overlap covers 318 open PRs (04:59:29 UTC), 4,077 discussion records (05:00:22 UTC), and all 6,636 current-base notes. Scoped matching/sublayer and downset/allocation queries identify the credited explicit predecessor obligations and this round's claims; no exhaustive novelty assertion is made. A separate verifier-agent review checked the actual source allocation/leaf/shear/plan, FULL-PROOF perturbation and generator contracts, all 11 input pins, exact one-expression AST equivalence, and independent noncommuting rational prefix/suffix inverse checks, with no blocker.
